tasks.title: 5. Meta app setup (yours)
tasks.detail:
YOUR STEPS — plain words, verified against Meta's official docs (2026-09-27):

BEFORE YOU START — check these two things:
• Your Instagram (@the_intelligently_artificial) is a Professional account (Business or Creator), not personal. Check in the Instagram app: Settings > Account type.
• That Instagram is linked to your Facebook Page, and your personal Facebook account is an admin of that Page.

REGISTER AS A DEVELOPER FIRST (you are on this page now):
1. Finish the signup: verify your phone number (they text you a code), then contact info, then about you.
   • If the page rejects your number: it must be added through Accounts Center first — go to Accounts Center > Personal details > Contact info and add it there.
   • If it's already listed there: tap the number row to confirm/verify it if offered, then refresh the developer page and continue.
   • Last resort: the developer page also lets you verify with a credit card instead (link at the bottom).
2. Only after that does the "My Apps" menu appear.

CREATE THE APP:
3. Open My Apps, then Create app.
4. Enter an app name (e.g. "Intelligently Artificial Publisher") and your contact email.
5. When it asks for use cases, select BOTH:
   • "Manage messaging & content on Instagram" (lets the app publish to Instagram)
   • "Manage everything on your Page" (lets the app publish to your Facebook Page)
6. YOUR STEPS — get the token, then store it:
   • Generate the token: in the app dashboard's left menu, open Instagram > API setup with Instagram business login, click Generate token next to your Instagram account (@the_intelligently_artificial), log into Instagram if asked, and copy the token. Per Meta's docs this token is long-lived (valid 60 days).
   • Store it: open this secure link and paste the token there (it goes straight to secure storage, never shown in chat):
     https://agent.meta.ai/connect/api-key?service=meta&&session_id=ac30e921-b994-4f0f-9fcb-502690b2c302
7. (Assistant, after the token.) I'll confirm instagram_business_content_publish is granted from the token itself; the publish test proves it.
8. (Assistant, after the token.) I'll confirm pages_manage_posts the same way.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT:
• When you reply "done", I take it from there.
• Then I run the two publish tests: one video to your Facebook Page, one reel to Instagram — through your app.

NOTE:
• Your app's overview screen confirmed "No requirements for the use cases on this app" — no App Review or business verification needed. Resolved 2026-09-27.

tasks.title: Review: repo-write enforcement strategy (yours)
tasks.detail:
Review my suggestions for enforcing the pull-before-code agreement across all repos, then agree on a strategy with me.
• Where we are: the pull-before-code rule is written down but nothing enforces it — I follow it by hand. Commits already go through the GitHub API, which refuses to overwrite a file that changed since I read it (fingerprint check).
• Option 1 — pre-edit check script: prints a sync receipt before edits. Still relies on me remembering to run it.
• Option 2 — drift-watch cron: reports any clone behind origin/main. Detection only, not prevention.
• Option 3 (my recommendation) — save through the API, not the clone: read the file from GitHub, edit, write back with its fingerprint. GitHub itself rejects stale writes, so staleness becomes impossible by construction. The local clone stays as scratch only.
• Open question: a small get/edit/put helper script so the read and fingerprint always come from one call.
Reply with the strategy you want, or your own variant. | Verdict 2026-09-29 (BalRam, in writing): approved.

tasks.title: Review: completed automation (yours)
tasks.detail:
Completed automation — ready for your review. Built tonight after the board-redesign approval unblocked it.

What it does:
- Phase 1 applies your verdict: a blocked_completed task whose review task is done with 'Verdict: approved' moves to completed; 'Verdict: rejected' moves it to not_approved. A done review with no verdict line is never guessed at — reported for a human.
